slug: 2026-03-01 Rising Repression Meets Global Resistance Internet Shutdowns in 2025

facts.fact: Access Now (#KeepItOn) reports a five-day nationwide internet blackout in Tanzania during the disputed 29 October 2025 election; the document does not name who ordered it, and gives no end date beyond the five days.
Access Now (#KeepItOn) counts 8 internet shutdowns in Tanzania in 2025, the highest of any African country in its report, of which the document describes only the election-time blackout.

note: Document also says the ACHPR condemned Tanzania's shutdown and that satellite (Starlink) orders occurred in Tanzania, undated and without detail; no fact taken.

facts.fact: The Legal & Human Rights Centre alleges in a case filed at the East African Court of Justice on 8 December 2025 that the Tanzanian government carried out a total nationwide internet shutdown from 29 October to 4 November 2025, cutting mobile data, websites and online platforms; this is the applicant's allegation, no judgment is recorded.
facts.system: Nationwide internet shutdown, 29 October to 4 November 2025

note: No judgment or verdict is given, so nothing for connection:barred.

facts.fact: The Tanzania Communications Regulatory Authority suspended the online content licence of Vapper Tech Limited (JamiiForums) for 90 days from 6 September 2025 over content it called misleading and insulting to the Government and the President, under the Online Content Regulations 2020, 2022 and 2025; it did not disclose the specific content.
The TCRA notice states it blocked access to the JamiiForums platform when it suspended the licence on 6 September 2025, for 90 days.

note: Meta disabled the accounts of a US-based critic in December 2025 and she alleges TCRA pressure; a takedown request, not a government-ordered cut, and published from abroad, so no fact.

facts.fact: The complaint filed 21 August 2026 states that the Tanzanian government shut down the internet nationwide around the 29 October 2025 election and protests; this is the plaintiff's allegation, with no end date given.

The complaint states that in the lead-up to the October 2025 election Tanzanian authorities blocked the platforms where Tanzanians could still speak freely, without naming them; this is the plaintiff's allegation.
facts.system: blocked online platforms before the 2025 election

facts.fact: The complaint states that in the lead-up to the October 2025 election the leader of the opposition was jailed on capital charges for calling for electoral reforms; this is the plaintiff's allegation, and no law is named.
facts.system: opposition leader jailed on capital charges

note: Abductions of critics and the Attorney General's vow to arrest the plaintiff are not arrests or charges for speech; the account takedown is a takedown request (other). Complaint text is an excerpt (introduction only).
Licences and licence fees for online publishers are other; no cut, arrest, criticism or repeal stated.
Abstract only, on online gender-based violence against women candidates; states no cut, punishment, repeal or government criticism.

facts.fact: The Internet Governance Project says Tanzania's framework of content licensing, VPN registration and internet shutdowns cost an estimated US$250 million in losses during the 2025 election period alone.
facts.system: internet shutdowns in the 2025 election period

note: Think-tank analysis; the shutdown is stated without who ordered it, which area or when it ended.

facts.fact: The Research ICT Africa report says Tanzania's information flows during the 2025 electoral cycle faced state-led internet shutdowns; it names no service, area, date or ordering body, so the year 2025 is the event date given.

note: Report is otherwise general (censorship, media capture, disinformation) with no named critic, arrest or closure, so no debate or penalty fact.

facts.fact: Amnesty International says Tanzania's authorities imposed a partial internet shutdown during the October 2025 general elections.

Amnesty International says the Tanzania Communications Regulatory Authority imposed a 90-day ban on JamiiForums in September 2025, alleging it published misleading and defamatory content about the government.
The Southern Africa Litigation Centre says the network was switched off around Tanzania's 2025 general election and the protests that followed.

note: Source does not say whose order; dated to the year only.
Nothing on public discussion, cuts or punishment.
The Arusha Declaration names no government policy, bill or decision criticised, and no cut or punishment is stated.
Grant record for digital-rights advocacy; no criticism of a named policy, cut or punishment stated.
Online content licensing and fee rules only; nothing a study asks.

facts.fact: Context reports the Tanzanian government restricted internet access nationwide from 29 October 2025 when polls opened, blocking Facebook, WhatsApp and other platforms; NetBlocks said services were restored on 3 November with social media restrictions remaining.
Access Now says Tanzania shut down the internet eight times in 2025, including twice during the election period.
Human Rights Watch says the government imposed nationwide internet restrictions in response to election-day protests in October 2025.
Human Rights Watch says the government blocked access to X in May 2025, and that TCRA had shut over 80,000 websites, accounts and platforms.
Human Rights Watch says TCRA suspended the web forum JamiiForums for 90 days in September 2025 for allegedly publishing content that insulted and disrespected the government and the President.
CPJ states that the state responded to post-election protests around the 29 October 2025 vote amid a five-day internet blackout.
CPJ states that in May 2025 authorities blocked access to X after the police account was hacked to announce the president's death, later saying the block was because X hosted pornography.
CPJ reports that ACT Wazalendo leader Janeth Rithe was arrested in June 2025 for telling supporters that the ruling party was running a police state.

note: Treason charge against journalist Godfrey Ng'omba and the arrests of Kusaga and others: the source does not say what they said, so no fact; the January 2025 ISP filtering rule is a power, not a cut.

facts.fact: Global Voices says Tanzania cut the internet during its October 2025 election.

note: Stakeholder input to a draft is not criticism of a named policy, and no cut or punishment is stated.

facts.fact: The EastAfrican says Tanzania's internet and communication slowdowns around major political and judicial events, such as the 6 November 2026 sentencing of Chadema leader Tundu Lissu, are part of a recurring pattern of state-managed bandwidth throttling.
